title: What does OracleDelete do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of OracleDelete and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, OracleDelete removes an account-owned price-oracle entry identified by its document identifier. [1]

Deleting the oracle stops that ledger entry from serving as a current publication; it does not erase prior price updates from history. Check ownership and OracleDocumentID rather than identifying a feed only by its display name. A deleted feed and a temporarily stale feed require different handling by applications that consume market data. [1]

The OracleDelete reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using OracleDelete, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
